label: token right after an early "p" (p at original position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires in the original phase at step 1 or 2 when the previous input was "p", meaning the first or second original token is "p". It does not depend on the current input token. Magnitude is highest (about 0.97-1.0 of max) when p is the very first token (step 1) and lower (about 0.73-0.85) when p is at position 1 (step 2). A p at position 2 gives only negligible activations (<0.1 of max) at step 3, and later p tokens give none. It never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase (9 tiny activations), including when p is fed back during copying. Dev split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99, mass recall 0.9998.

issues: Only minor and negligible: about 226 test steps at t=3 (p at original position 1, i.e. the third original token) carry tiny activations (<=0.08 of max, about 0% of activation mass). The explanation already says this.

The 9 copy-phase activations (t=5, recall_idx 2, prev_tok f/u/c/q/digits, not p) are scattered noise. All 33,560 activations with prev_tok==p fall in the original phase, so 'never fires when p is fed back during copying' holds.

The magnitude claims hold: t=1 after p is about 0.97-1.00 (top examples are 'p e ...' at 1.00), and t=2 after p is about 0.73-0.85 in the low and second quartiles. The input token has a flat distribution (about 0.035 mass share each).
